Subject: Re: Production: sudden live-chat disconnects and 429 spikes

Karthik / team — quick triage:

Summary of findings so far (15:42 PT):
- We see a pattern where long-lived streaming sessions are being torn down by idle-timeout enforcement at the edge layer after ~12s of no bytes sent, despite clients still being attached: likely a change in our edge keepalive default that rolled out in the 03:00 UTC deploy window.
- When clients retry immediately (client SDKs do exponential backoff but many implement aggressive reattempts), request rates hit our token quota filters and edge throttles returning 429s; under load a small subset of server-side gRPC handlers return 500 due to KV cache eviction pressure on the conversation state store.

Immediate mitigations we pushed (15:30 PT):
- Reverted the 03:00 UTC edge keepalive change in the Canary pool (rollback complete).
- Temporarily increased the per-connection idle timeout to 30s at the edge for Novus-specific routes.
- Bumped token quota thresholds for the affected routes to reduce 429 churn while we stabilize.

Next steps:
- Run a 30 min canary and monitor 5xx/429 and idle-disconnect metrics.
- Produce a short postmortem with timeline and recommended long-term config: tweak keepalive heuristics, improve client SDK jitter/backoff guidance, and add per-customer circuit-breaker smoothing.

I've uploaded the raw diagnostic snippet to the incident: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-4729
Attached are the logs we pulled from the canary pool.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
SRE, Redwood Inference

Dana — quick exec-summary and actions from our end:

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Incident began ~07:30 UTC on 2026-11-14 after an edge keepalive/idle timeout change deployed in the 03:00 UTC release window. That change caused premature stream termination for several long-polling chat sessions. Client retries amplified requests, producing a 429 surge; under the surge a small fraction of streaming handlers returned 5xx due to conversation-state cache contention.

Actions completed (Nov 14):
- Canary rollback of keepalive change (03:30 UTC)
- Edge idle timeout increased to 30s for Novus routes (temporary)
- Token quota thresholds raised for affected routes to absorb retry bursts
- Monitoring dashboards updated (per-route 429/5xx and idle disconnect rate)

Planned follow-up:
- Incident postmortem with timeline and recommendations (target: 11/18)
- Client SDK guidance published for better retry backoff and jitter (target: 11/20)
- Add per-customer smoothing circuit to reduce hard throttle surfaces (Q1 roadmap)

SLA credit guidance: If the incident exceeds 4 hours of service-effecting impact we will offer a pro-rated credit per contract terms; I'll coordinate with Finance & Legal to produce an estimate for Novus by Monday EOD.

Proposed exec sync: Mon, 16 Nov at 10:00 AM ET (30 minutes). Please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite.
